glyph_origin: According to Shuowen, phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 能 (“bear”) + abbreviated phonetic 炎. This character originally represented an onomatopoetic word (熊熊 (“(of flame) raging”)). Later its semantic component 能, the character for the Old Chinese word "bear", was borrowed for another word. This character thus began to represent the word "bear" instead.
shuowen: According to Shuowen, phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 能 (“bear”) + abbreviated phonetic 炎.
senses: [xióng] (archaic, Muping Mandarin, &, Xining Mandarin, Xinzhou Jin) black bear
